theme_scores.justification: The lines on the two-year window, the Finance Bill 2017 and the technical consultation are assertions and plans with no evidence for why this timetable or route was chosen and no citation.

The lines on nine categories, per-100g targets, the 2015 baseline and the nutrient profile review describe measures and give reasoning ("Some companies have led the way") but no data, finding or source showing why these categories, targets or timings were chosen.
The lines on Ofsted inspection, the PHE advice, the online tool, County Sports Partnerships and the rating scheme describe mechanisms with no evidence that they will work and no references.
The lines on the Children's Food Trust menus, the campaign and the framework update describe commitments with no evidence or references.

reasoning: All three core themes sit at level 0, so the mean is 0 and the section score is 0. The extract has empty reference and link blocks throughout, and none of the lines offers a statistic, research finding, named dataset, consultation response or comparable policy as grounds for how the levy and programme will be delivered. In "Levy delivery and timetable", the line "We have given producers and importers two years to lower the sugar in their drinks" sets out a timetable without saying why two years was chosen or what it rests on. In "Public Health England-led reduction programme", the nine categories are said to be those "that make the largest contributions to children's sugar intakes", and the footnote marker "ii" is embedded in the prose, but no figure or source is shown and no reference is attached. The reasoning that early reformulators deserve recognition justifies the 2015 baseline only as an argument. In "School delivery mechanisms", the Ofsted lines describe procedures, not evidence they will raise activity or improve food. The strongest counter-example to level 0 is the claim about the nine categories, which implies an underlying dataset on children's sugar intake. However, it is unnamed and unexplained here, and the extract gives no figures. To reach level 1, the document would need to state the evidence behind its choices, such as intake shares by category or the basis for the two-year window. To reach level 2, it would need to cite those sources.
